title: GlobalProtect / AnyConnect VPN Disconnection & Authentication Issues
summary: Step-by-step guide to diagnose and fix frequent VPN disconnections, invalid certificate errors, and MFA prompt loops.
content:
Symptoms:
- VPN disconnects every few minutes or fails to initialize authentication tunnel.
- Error message: 'Gateway not reachable' or 'Certificate validation failed'.

Troubleshooting Steps:
1. Verify local internet connectivity by pinging 8.8.8.8 and company portal.
2. Open VPN client settings, select 'Refresh Connection', and reconnect.
3. Clear DNS cache: Run Command Prompt as Admin and execute `ipconfig /flushdns`.
4. Reset Network Adapter: Go to Settings > Network & Internet > Advanced network settings > Network reset.
5. If MFA is stuck, re-authenticate via the Authenticator app or request MFA token reset.
6. Check firewall rules to ensure UDP ports 4500 and 500 are allowed.

title: Windows Blue Screen of Death (BSOD) & Stop Code Diagnosis
summary: Resolving system crashes, dump file analysis, and common BSOD stop codes like CRITICAL_PROCESS_DIED and DRIVER_IRQL_NOT_LESS_OR_EQUAL.
content:
Symptoms:
- System crashes unexpectedly showing a blue screen with a stop code and restarts.

Troubleshooting Steps:
1. Note the specific stop code (e.g., PAGE_FAULT_IN_NONPAGED_AREA, DRIVER_IRQL_NOT_LESS_OR_EQUAL).
2. Boot Windows into Safe Mode (Hold Shift while clicking Restart > Troubleshoot > Startup Settings > Safe Mode).
3. Check recent software or driver updates. Uninstall recently installed display or graphics drivers via Device Manager.
4. System File Inspection: Run `sfc /scannow` and `DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /RestoreHealth` in Admin CMD.
5. Memory Health Test: Run `mdsched.exe` (Windows Memory Diagnostic) to check RAM integrity.
6. Check system temperature and disk health using diagnostic tools. If hardware failure is suspected, open an urgent hardware ticket.

title: Wi-Fi Connectivity, IP Conflict & DNS Resolution Errors
summary: How to resolve 'No Internet, Secured', DNS probe finished errors, and wireless network dropping.
content:
Symptoms:
- Laptop connected to Wi-Fi but shows 'No Internet Access' or browser shows DNS failure.

Troubleshooting Steps:
1. Toggle Airplane mode ON for 5 seconds, then OFF.
2. Forget the Wi-Fi network and reconnect using network credentials.
3. Release and Renew IP Address:
   - Open CMD as Admin.
   - Execute `ipconfig /release` followed by `ipconfig /renew`.
4. Change DNS servers to Google DNS (8.8.8.8 / 8.8.4.4) or Cloudflare DNS (1.1.1.1) in IPv4 properties.
5. Restart Wireless Network Service: Run `net stop wlansvc` and `net start wlansvc` in Admin CMD.

title: Microsoft Outlook Synchronization & Profile Corruption Fix
summary: Fix Outlook stuck on 'Disconnected', OST file corruption, and email sending failure.
content:
Symptoms:
- Emails not sending/receiving, Outlook stuck on 'Updating Inbox' or 'Disconnected'.

Troubleshooting Steps:
1. Verify Outlook status bar at the bottom right. If Offline, switch to 'Send / Receive' tab and click 'Work Offline' to toggle online mode.
2. Run Outlook in Safe Mode: Press `Win + R`, type `outlook.exe /safe` and press Enter.
3. Repair Office Installation: Control Panel > Programs and Features > Select Microsoft 365 > Click Change > Quick Repair.
4. Rebuild Outlook Profile: Control Panel > Mail > Show Profiles > Add new profile and set as default.
5. Compact / Repair OST file: Locate OST file in `%localappdata%\Microsoft\Outlook` and run `SCANPST.EXE`.

title: Account Lockout & Self-Service Password Reset (SSPR) Workflow
summary: Instructions for unlocking Active Directory domain accounts and completing self-service password reset.
content:
Symptoms:
- 'Your account has been locked out. Please contact your administrator' message on login.

Troubleshooting Steps:
1. Wait 15 minutes for automatic lockout timer expiration (if enabled by organization policy).
2. Use the Self-Service Password Reset (SSPR) portal at https://passwordreset.microsoftonline.com.
3. Trigger automated account verification via IT Helpdesk Agent tool: command `trigger_password_reset` with username.
4. Disconnect phone/mobile devices from corporate Wi-Fi temporarily to stop outdated saved passwords from triggering re-lockouts.
5. If SSPR fails, contact IT service desk with Employee ID for identity verification.

title: High CPU / Memory Usage & System Performance Optimization
summary: Diagnosing background processes consuming 100% CPU/RAM and optimizing Windows workstation speed.
content:
Symptoms:
- Workstation freezing, fans spinning loud, slow response time when opening apps.

Troubleshooting Steps:
1. Open Task Manager (`Ctrl + Shift + Esc`) and sort processes by CPU and Memory usage.
2. Identify rogue processes (e.g., SearchIndexer, Windows Update loop, hung browser sub-processes).
3. End high-resource non-essential background processes.
4. Disable unnecessary Startup programs under Task Manager > Startup tab.
5. Run system diagnostic check to inspect total available physical memory and free disk space.
6. Clear temporary files: Open Run (`Win + R`), type `%temp%` and delete temporary files.

title: Network Printer Offline & Print Spooler Service Reset
summary: Fixing printer offline errors, clearing print queue jams, and restarting the Print Spooler service.
content:
Symptoms:
- Print jobs stuck in queue with status 'Error - Printing' or printer shows 'Offline'.

Troubleshooting Steps:
1. Verify physical connection / IP connection of printer. Ping printer IP address.
2. Restart Print Spooler Service:
   - Run CMD as Administrator.
   - Type `net stop spooler` and press Enter.
   - Delete queue files in `C:\Windows\System32\spool\PRINTERS`.
   - Type `net start spooler` and press Enter.
3. Check Windows Settings > Devices > Printers & Scanners > Open Queue > Printer > Uncheck 'Use Printer Offline'.
4. Re-add printer using printer IP address or hostname.

title: Local Administrative Rights & Software Installation Policy
summary: Guidelines and request procedures for software installations requiring elevated permissions.
content:
Symptoms:
- Prompted for administrator credentials (UAC prompt) when installing company-approved software.

Troubleshooting Steps:
1. Check if the required software is available in Company Portal / Software Center (does not require admin password).
2. If installing standard utilities (e.g., VS Code, Git, Docker, Node.js), verify if user-scoped installers are available.
3. If local admin rights are required for development or system administration, submit a Temporary Admin Request ticket with business justification.
4. All unauthorized executable files (.exe / .msi) are subject to automated endpoint protection scanning.
